category: Classify Flouroquinolones
front: Distinguish between the two types of plasmid-mediated resistance to fluoroquinolones: Qnr proteins and modified acetyltransferase.
back:
• Qnr proteins: Protect the target enzymes (DNA gyrase) from drug binding.
• Modified acetyltransferase: A variant enzyme capable of inactivating ciprofloxacin specifically.

category: Classify Flouroquinolones
front: Which fluoroquinolone is the notable exception to the rule of requiring dosage adjustment in renal failure?
back:
Moxifloxacin.
• It is eliminated via non-renal (hepatic/biliary) pathways.
• All other systemic quinolones require adjustment for creatinine clearance < 50 mL/min.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: The primary four-drug intensive phase for treating drug-susceptible tuberculosis includes Isoniazid, Rifampin, Pyrazinamide, and [___].
back:
- Ethambutol
- These represent first-line antituberculosis agents
- Chosen for maximum efficacy and acceptable toxicity
- Standard initial therapy for 8 weeks

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: A 50-year-old patient on a standard 1st-line TB regimen develops difficulty distinguishing red from green colors. This toxicity is specifically associated with the [___] medication in the regimen.
back:
- Ethambutol
- Causes dose-related retrobulbar neuritis
- Requires baseline visual acuity and color testing
- Classified as a traditional first-line agent

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Explain the molecular mechanism by which the first-line agent Isoniazid (INH) inhibits the growth of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
back:
- Inhibits synthesis of mycolic acids (essential cell wall components)
- Requires activation by mycobacterial catalase-peroxidase (KatG)
- Blocks the enzyme KasA and acyl carrier protein AcpM

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Contrast the clinical selection criteria for utilizing first-line versus second-line antituberculosis agents.
back:
- First-line: Used for drug-susceptible TB; high efficacy and acceptable toxicity
- Second-line: Reserved for resistance (MDR-TB), treatment failure, or severe first-line intolerance
- Second-line drugs are often less effective or more toxic

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
coreConcept: Role of Pyrazinamide in TB Therapy
front: Identify the first-line agent used specifically during the 2-month intensive phase as a 'sterilizing' drug active against residual intracellular organisms.
back:
- Pyrazinamide (PZA)
- Active against bacilli in acidic environments (lysosomes)
- Reduces total treatment duration to 6 months
- Major toxicity: Hepatotoxicity and hyperuricemia

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: The traditional 1st-line agent [___] acts by binding to the β-subunit of bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, thereby inhibiting RNA synthesis.
back:
- Rifampin
- Potent inducer of cytochrome P450 enzymes
- Bactericidal against extracellular and intracellular organisms
- Causes orange discoloration of urine/tears

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: A patient diagnosed with multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) requires an injectable agent. Name two second-line injectable options available for this therapy.
back:
- Amikacin
- Capreomycin
- (Streptomycin is another second-line injectable option)
- Used when 1st-line oral agents fail due to resistance

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Describe the unique biological target of the second-line drug Bedaquiline and its primary clinical role.
back:
- Inhibits mycobacterial ATP synthase
- Active against both replicating and nonreplicating bacilli
- Reserved for adults with pulmonary MDR-TB when other options fail

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Contrast Rifampin and Rifabutin regarding their use in tuberculosis patients receiving protease-inhibitor-based antiretroviral therapy for HIV.
back:
- Rifampin: Potent CYP450 inducer; contraindicated (significantly lowers PI levels)
- Rifabutin: Less potent CYP inducer; preferred 2nd-line alternative to allow concomitant PI use

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: List four examples of oral second-line antituberculosis agents that are not fluoroquinolones.
back:
- Ethionamide
- Cycloserine
- Aminosalicylic acid (PAS)
- Linezolid
- Used specifically for resistant or complicated TB cases

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: The standard four-drug intensive phase for treating drug-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis consists of the primary 1st-line agents Isoniazid, Rifampin, Pyrazinamide, and [___].
back:
• Ethambutol
• Acts as a bacteriostatic agent
• Prevents emergence of resistance to other 1st-line drugs during initial treatment.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: A 30-year-old patient with pulmonary TB shows clinical failure after 3 months. Sensitivity testing confirms resistance to Isoniazid and Rifampin. To manage this Multidrug-Resistant (MDR) case, therapy must shift to [___].
back:
• 2nd-line agents
• Examples: Bedaquiline, Moxifloxacin, Amikacin, or Linezolid
• Reserved for resistance or severe toxicity to 1st-line drugs.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism of action of the 1st-line agent Isoniazid (INH).
back:
• Inhibits mycolic acid synthesis
• Essential for mycobacterial cell wall integrity
• Activated by the viral enzyme KatG (catalase-peroxidase).

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Contrast the primary rationale for using 1st-line antituberculosis agents versus 2nd-line agents.
back:
• 1st-line: High efficacy and acceptable toxicity; used for standard drug-susceptible cases.
• 2nd-line: Lower efficacy or higher toxicity; reserved for drug resistance or 1st-line failure.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Categorize Ethionamide and Para-aminosalicylic acid (PAS) according to their clinical priority in TB treatment.
back:
• 2nd-line agents
• Ethionamide: Blocks mycolic acid synthesis (similar to INH)
• PAS: Folate synthesis antagonist (similar to sulfonamides).

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: In the management of Multidrug-Resistant (MDR) tuberculosis, the specific 2nd-line injectable peptide antibiotic utilized is [___].
back:
• Capreomycin
• Inhibits protein synthesis
• Essential when aminoglycoside resistance is suspected in 2nd-line regimens.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: A patient on standard 1st-line TB therapy develops visual acuity loss and red-green color blindness. Identify the drug responsible and the class of agent to be substituted if resistance occurs.
back:
• Responsible drug: Ethambutol (1st-line)
• Substitution class: 2nd-line agents
• Potential substitutes: Fluoroquinolones (e.g., Moxifloxacin) or injectables.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Describe the unique mechanism of action associated with the novel 2nd-line agent Bedaquiline.
back:
• Inhibits mycobacterial ATP synthase
• Disrupts energy production in the cell
• Active against both replicating and non-replicating bacilli.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Contrast 1st-line Rifampin with 2nd-line Rifapentine regarding their dosing frequency in the continuation phase of therapy.
back:
• Rifampin: Daily or thrice-weekly dosing (Standard 1st-line)
• Rifapentine: Once-weekly dosing (Alternative 2nd-line for select cases)
• Both are potent CYP450 inducers.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Identify the two most active 1st-line drugs that form the backbone of therapy for susceptible tuberculosis.
back:
• Isoniazid and Rifampin
• Combination cures 95–98% of susceptible cases
• Usually administered for a total of 6 to 9 months.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: The cornerstone drug of tuberculosis therapy, which acts as a prodrug activated by the mycobacterial catalase-peroxidase enzyme KatG, is [___].
back:
• Isoniazid (INH)
• Primary first-line agent
• Inhibits mycolic acid synthesis
• Bactericidal against actively growing bacilli

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: A 45-year-old patient on the intensive phase of TB treatment complains of decreased visual acuity and red-green color blindness. The drug responsible is [___].
back:
• Ethambutol
• First-line agent
• Causes dose-related retrobulbar neuritis
• Requires baseline and monthly visual testing

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which Rifampin inhibits Mycobacterium tuberculosis replication.
back:
• Binds to the beta-subunit of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
• Inhibits bacterial RNA synthesis
• Bactericidal for mycobacteria
• Potent inducer of CYP450 enzymes

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Contrast the use of Rifampin and Rifabutin in patients co-infected with HIV and Tuberculosis.
back:
• Rifampin: Potent CYP450 inducer; significantly lowers levels of Protease Inhibitors and NNRTIs
• Rifabutin: Preferred in HIV; less potent CYP450 induction; allows more stable antiretroviral dosing

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Identify the primary second-line fluoroquinolones used for resistant tuberculosis and their basic mechanism.
back:
• Levofloxacin and Moxifloxacin
• Inhibit DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) and topoisomerase IV
• Used when resistance to first-line agents occurs

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Multidrug-resistant (MDR) tuberculosis is defined specifically as laboratory-confirmed resistance to both [___] and [___].
back:
• Isoniazid
• Rifampin
• Requires use of second-line agents like Bedaquiline or Amikacin

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: A patient with MDR-TB is started on an oral diarylquinoline that inhibits mycobacterial ATP synthase. This second-line agent is [___].
back:
• Bedaquiline
• Novel mechanism: Inhibits ATP synthase
• Targets both replicating and dormant bacilli
• Boxed warning: QTc prolongation

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: How does Pyrazinamide function differently from other first-line agents in the intensive phase of treatment?
back:
• Acts as a "sterilizing agent"
• Targets residual intracellular organisms in acidic macrophage lysosomes
• Essential for shortening total treatment to 6 months

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Contrast Streptomycin and Capreomycin regarding their classification and use in TB.
back:
• Streptomycin: Aminoglycoside; first-line (historical) or second-line injectable; targets protein synthesis (30S)
• Capreomycin: Peptide antibiotic; second-line injectable; essential for drug-resistant cases

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: List the four agents that constitute the standard first-line intensive phase regimen for drug-susceptible tuberculosis.
back:
• Isoniazid (INH)
• Rifampin (RIF)
• Pyrazinamide (PZA)
• Ethambutol (EMB)

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: The four primary first-line antituberculosis agents used in the initial intensive phase of treatment are Isoniazid, Rifampin, Pyrazinamide, and [___].
back:
● Ethambutol.
● These are prioritized due to high efficacy and acceptable toxicity.
● Standard short-course therapy (RHEZ) utilizes this combination for drug-susceptible strains.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: A 45-year-old male with pulmonary TB develops resistance to Isoniazid and Rifampin. He is started on a diarylquinoline that inhibits ATP synthase. This drug is classified as a [___] agent.
back:
● Second-line agent (Bedaquiline).
● Reserved for multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB).
● Specifically indicated when other treatment options are exhausted due to QTc prolongation risk.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Explain the pharmacological rationale for classifying Pyrazinamide as a first-line 'sterilizing' agent.
back:
● Targets semi-dormant mycobacteria in acidic environments (macrophage lysosomes).
● Highly effective at preventing disease relapse.
● Essential for shortening total treatment duration to 6 months.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Contrast the clinical classification and utility of Streptomycin versus Capreomycin in tuberculosis management.
back:
● Streptomycin: Aminoglycoside; historically first-line, now often classified as a second-line injectable.
● Capreomycin: Cyclic peptide; strictly second-line; used for MDR-TB resistant to aminoglycosides.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: List three examples of second-line oral bacteriostatic agents used in resistant tuberculosis.
back:
● Ethionamide.
● Cycloserine.
● Para-aminosalicylic acid (PAS).
● These are used when first-line agents fail or cause significant toxicity.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: [___] is a first-line antituberculosis drug that acts by inhibiting mycobacterial arabinosyl transferase, thereby disrupting cell wall polymerization.
back:
● Ethambutol.
● Classified as a bacteriostatic first-line agent.
● Used to prevent resistance emergence if the strain is resistant to Isoniazid.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: A patient with multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) requires a second-line protein synthesis inhibitor. Identify the classification and common adverse profile of Linezolid in this setting.
back:
● Second-line oxazolidinone agent.
● Side effects: Bone marrow suppression (thrombocytopenia), peripheral neuropathy, and optic neuritis.
● Requires supplemental pyridoxine during long-term use.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: How does the classification and drug-interaction profile of Rifabutin differ from Rifampin for TB patients with HIV?
back:
● Both are first-line rifamycins.
● Rifabutin is preferred in HIV patients on protease inhibitors.
● Rationale: Rifabutin is a less potent inducer of CYP450 enzymes.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
coreConcept: Priority and Bactericidal vs Bacteriostatic Classification
front: Contrast the use of first-line Ethambutol with second-line Fluoroquinolones (e.g., Moxifloxacin) in TB therapy.
back:
● Ethambutol: Standard first-line bacteriostatic; targets cell wall.
● Fluoroquinolones: Potent second-line bactericidal; targets DNA gyrase; reserved for resistant strains or intolerance.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Identify the first-line antituberculosis drug that specifically requires activation by the mycobacterial catalase-peroxidase enzyme KatG.
back:
● Isoniazid (INH).
● Primary first-line bactericidal prodrug.
● Mechanism: Inhibits mycolic acid synthesis once activated by KatG.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: The standard intensive phase of short-course chemotherapy for drug-susceptible tuberculosis typically includes the four first-line agents: Isoniazid, Rifampin, Pyrazinamide, and [___].
back:
• Ethambutol
• Note: These four drugs form the "RIPE" regimen used for the first 2 months of treatment.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: A patient with multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) is started on a regimen containing an injectable second-line agent that inhibits protein synthesis and is obtained from *Streptomyces capreolus*. Identify this drug.
back:
• Capreomycin
• It is an important injectable second-line agent often used when there is resistance to first-line drugs.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
coreConcept: Role of Pyrazinamide in TB therapy
front: Explain the pharmacological role of Pyrazinamide as a "sterilizing agent" in the 6-month first-line TB treatment regimen.
back:
• Acts against residual intracellular organisms residing in acidic environments (macrophage lysosomes).
• Its inclusion allows the total duration of therapy to be reduced from 9 months to 6 months.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Contrast the clinical utility of Streptomycin with that of Amikacin within the current classification of antituberculosis drugs.
back:
• Streptomycin: Historically first-line, now a second-line injectable used primarily when other drugs are unavailable or for specific resistant strains.
• Amikacin: A potent second-line injectable reserved for MDR-TB, maintaining activity against many streptomycin-resistant strains.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: List three second-line oral antitubercular drugs that are primarily used only when there is resistance to first-line agents or treatment failure.
back:
• Ethionamide
• Cycloserine
• Aminosalicylic acid (PAS)

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: [___] is a novel second-line diarylquinoline that acts by inhibiting ATP synthase in both replicating and non-replicating mycobacteria, specifically reserved for MDR-TB.
back:
• Bedaquiline
• It carries a black-box warning for QTc prolongation and increased mortality risk.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: A patient with HIV is undergoing treatment for pulmonary tuberculosis. To avoid severe drug interactions with protease inhibitors, which first-line rifamycin is often substituted for Rifampin?
back:
• Rifabutin
• It is a less potent inducer of cytochrome P450 enzymes compared to Rifampin.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Describe the physiological mechanism by which Ethionamide acts as a second-line agent and state its relationship to Isoniazid cross-resistance.
back:
• Inhibits mycolic acid synthesis (similar to Isoniazid).
• Cross-resistance occurs with low-level Isoniazid resistance (inhA mutations), but may be active against high-level katG mutants.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Contrast the biochemical targets of the first-line agent Ethambutol and the second-line agent Cycloserine.
back:
• Ethambutol: Inhibits arabinosyl transferases (blocks polymerization of arabinoglycan in cell wall).
• Cycloserine: Structural analog of D-alanine; inhibits alanine racemase and D-alanyl-D-alanine ligase.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Name two fluoroquinolones categorized as second-line agents that are highly effective against Mycobacterium tuberculosis and used when first-line drugs fail.
back:
• Levofloxacin
• Moxifloxacin
• (Moxifloxacin is generally considered the most active in vitro).

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Standard short-course chemotherapy for drug-susceptible tuberculosis utilizes four primary first-line agents: Isoniazid, Rifampin, [___], and Ethambutol.
back:
• Pyrazinamide.
• First-line agents are defined by high efficacy and manageable toxicity.
• This combination is used during the 2-month intensive phase.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: A 45-year-old patient with pulmonary TB begins a regimen that causes harmless orange discoloration of his urine and tears. This drug belongs to which line of antituberculosis therapy?
back:
• First-line (Rifampin).
• Rifampin is a potent RNA polymerase inhibitor.
• Crucial for its bactericidal and sterilizing activity.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Explain the rationale for grouping the second-line agent Ethionamide with the first-line agent Isoniazid regarding their metabolic target.
back:
• Both inhibit mycolic acid synthesis.
• Both are structural analogs of nicotinamide.
• Ethionamide is reserved for resistance to first-line agents due to gastrointestinal intolerance.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Contrast first-line and second-line antituberculosis drugs regarding their therapeutic priority and efficacy-to-toxicity ratio.
back:
• First-line: Primary preference; highest efficacy and lowest toxicity for susceptible strains.
• Second-line: Reserved for multidrug-resistance (MDR-TB); exhibit lower efficacy, higher toxicity, or less established data.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Identify three injectable agents classified as second-line antituberculosis drugs according to current standard guidelines.
back:
• Streptomycin.
• Amikacin.
• Capreomycin.
• These are utilized when first-line oral regimens fail or resistance is confirmed.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Although historically part of primary therapy, [___] is now classified as a second-line agent due to widespread resistance and the risk of irreversible ototoxicity.
back:
• Streptomycin.
• It is an aminoglycoside that inhibits protein synthesis.
• Replaced by ethambutol in standard first-line oral therapy.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: A patient with confirmed MDR-TB is started on a newer second-line agent that selectively inhibits mycobacterial ATP synthase. Name this drug.
back:
• Bedaquiline.
• A diarylquinoline reserved for resistant cases.
• Associated with QTc prolongation and potential hepatotoxicity.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Describe the clinical role of Fluoroquinolones (e.g., Moxifloxacin or Levofloxacin) in the context of TB drug lines.
back:
• Classified as second-line agents.
• Used for multidrug-resistant TB or when first-line agents cause severe toxicity.
• Moxifloxacin is the most active in vitro.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Contrast the therapeutic status of Ethambutol versus Cycloserine in TB management.
back:
• Ethambutol: First-line; prevents resistance in primary 4-drug therapy.
• Cycloserine: Second-line; reserved for resistant cases due to severe CNS toxicity (psychosis/seizures).

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Which first-line antituberculosis agent is specifically utilized as a 'sterilizing agent' due to its activity against residual intracellular organisms in acidic environments?
back:
• Pyrazinamide.
• Active at pH 5.5 inside macrophage lysosomes.
• Key component of short-course (6-month) treatment regimens.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: The four primary drugs categorized as first-line agents for the treatment of drug-susceptible tuberculosis are Isoniazid, Rifampin, Pyrazinamide, and [___].
back:
• Ethambutol
• Completes the standard RIPE regimen
• Inhibits mycobacterial arabinosyl transferases to block cell wall synthesis

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: A patient with MDR-TB is started on a second-line injectable agent. Serial audiometry reveals significant high-frequency hearing loss. Identify the most likely drug class and a specific agent.
back:
• Class: Second-line injectable anti-TB agents
• Agent: Capreomycin (cyclic peptide) or Amikacin (aminoglycoside)
• Common toxicities: Ototoxicity (vestibular/auditory) and nephrotoxicity

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Explain the role of Pyrazinamide as a first-line "sterilizing" agent during the intensive phase of therapy.
back:
• Acts against semi-dormant bacilli in acidic environments (lysosomes)
• Facilitates shortening treatment duration from 9 to 6 months
• Active against intracellular organisms that may cause relapse

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Contrast the general therapeutic utility and toxicity profiles of first-line agents compared to second-line antituberculosis agents.
back:
• First-line: High efficacy, lower toxicity; used for induction and continuation in standard therapy
• Second-line: Lower efficacy, higher toxicity; reserved for MDR-TB or treatment-limiting adverse reactions

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Identify the specific molecular target of Bedaquiline, a recently approved second-line agent used for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis.
back:
• Target: Mycobacterial ATP synthase
• Effect: Inhibits energy production in both replicating and nonreplicating bacilli
• Black-box warning: Risk of QTc prolongation and increased mortality

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: To categorize a clinical isolate as Multidrug-Resistant Tuberculosis (MDR-TB), it must demonstrate resistance to the two potent first-line agents Isoniazid and [___].
back:
• Rifampin
• Necessitates the transition to a complex regimen of second-line drugs
• Standard MDR-TB treatment includes fluoroquinolones and injectable agents

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: A patient on TB therapy presents with red-green color blindness. This side effect is characteristic of which first-line agent, and what is its specific cellular target?
back:
• Agent: Ethambutol
• Target: Arabinosyl transferases (encoded by embCAB operon)
• Mechanism: Inhibits polymerization of arabinoglycan in the cell wall

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Describe the intracellular activation required for Isoniazid and the specific metabolic pathway it inhibits within the mycobacterium.
back:
• Activation: A prodrug activated by KatG (catalase-peroxidase)
• Target: InhA and KasA enzymes
• Effect: Inhibits mycolic acid synthesis, disrupting cell wall integrity

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Contrast Rifampin and Rifabutin regarding their induction of the cytochrome P450 system and the resulting clinical choice for HIV-coinfected patients.
back:
• Rifampin: Strong CYP inducer; significantly reduces Protease Inhibitor (PI) levels
• Rifabutin: Less potent inducer; preferred to minimize drug interactions with ART (Antiretroviral Therapy)

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: List three examples of second-line antituberculosis agents that are administered strictly via the oral route.
back:
• Ethionamide (inhibits mycolic acids)
• Cycloserine (cell wall synthesis inhibitor)
• Aminosalicylic acid (PAS; folate antagonist)

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: The metabolic clearance of Isoniazid is primarily determined by the genetically controlled rate of [___] in the liver.
back:
• Acetylation (by N-acetyltransferase 2).
• Determines 'fast' vs 'slow' acetylator status.
• Slow acetylators have higher drug levels and increased risk of peripheral neuropathy.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: A 45-year-old TB patient reports difficulty distinguishing between traffic light colors and blurred vision. The drug responsible for this inhibits [___].
back:
• Arabinosyl transferase.
• Disrupts polymerization of arabinoglycan in the mycobacterial cell wall.
• Causes dose-dependent retrobulbar neuritis (optic neuritis).

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Explain the molecular mechanism by which Rifampin inhibits mycobacterial growth.
back:
• Binds to the β-subunit of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase.
• Inhibits RNA synthesis (transcription).
• Bactericidal against intracellular and extracellular organisms.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Contrast the primary genetic loci involved in resistance against Isoniazid versus Rifampin.
back:
• Isoniazid: Mutations in katG (catalase-peroxidase) or inhA (acyl carrier protein reductase).
• Rifampin: Mutations in rpoB (β-subunit of RNA polymerase).
• Both mechanisms result in high-level clinical resistance.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Specify the most clinically significant pharmacokinetic property of Rifampin regarding drug-drug interactions.
back:
• Potent inducer of Cytochrome P450 (CYP3A4, 2C9, 2C19).
• Accelerates metabolism of oral contraceptives, warfarin, and HIV protease inhibitors.
• Often necessitates drug substitution or dosage adjustment.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Pyrazinamide is a prodrug that is converted to its active form, pyrazinoic acid, by the mycobacterial enzyme [___].
back:
• Pyrazinamidase (encoded by pncA).
• Conversion occurs preferentially under acidic conditions.
• Active against bacilli residing within macrophage lysosomes.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: A patient on antituberculous therapy presents with acute pain and swelling in the first metatarsophalangeal joint. Identify the drug-induced metabolic alteration responsible.
back:
• Inhibition of renal uric acid excretion.
• Leads to hyperuricemia (secondary gout).
• Primarily associated with Pyrazinamide therapy.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Explain the necessity of the KatG enzyme for Isoniazid's pharmacological activity.
back:
• Isoniazid is a prodrug.
• KatG (catalase-peroxidase) activates Isoniazid into an active radical form.
• Only the activated form inhibits mycolic acid synthesis via InhA blockage.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
coreConcept: Differential Environmental Activity of TB Drugs
front: Contrast Isoniazid and Pyrazinamide regarding the characteristic environmental pH required for optimal drug activity.
back:
• Isoniazid: Active at neutral pH against rapidly dividing extracellular bacilli.
• Pyrazinamide: Active at acidic pH (5.5) against intracellular bacilli in lysosomes.
• PZA acts as a 'sterilizing' agent to prevent relapse.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Describe the dose adjustment for Ethambutol in a patient with a creatinine clearance less than 30 mL/min.
back:
• Reduce frequency to three times weekly (rather than daily).
• Prevents drug accumulation as 50% is excreted unchanged in urine.
• Minimizes risk of irreversible ocular toxicity.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: The standard four-drug intensive phase regimen for drug-susceptible tuberculosis includes Isoniazid, Rifampin, Pyrazinamide, and [___].
back:
• Ethambutol.
• These constitute the 'RIPE' quartet.
• Essential for the initial 2-month intensive phase to prevent resistance.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: A patient with multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) is started on a newer diarylquinoline that inhibits bacterial ATP synthase. Name this agent and its primary cardiac toxicity.
back:
• Bedaquiline.
• QTc prolongation.
• Reserved for MDR-TB when other options are limited due to increased mortality risk.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Explain the role of Pyrazinamide as a first-line agent regarding its 'sterilizing' effect and target environment.
back:
• Targets dormant intracellular bacilli.
• Active in acidic environments (lysosomes).
• Allows the shortening of total treatment duration from 9 to 6 months.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Contrast the clinical indications for utilizing first-line antituberculosis agents versus second-line agents like Capreomycin or PAS.
back:
• First-line: Standard initial therapy for susceptible strains; high efficacy and lower toxicity.
• Second-line: Reserved for MDR-TB, treatment failure, or life-threatening drug intolerance.
• Second-line agents are generally less potent and more toxic.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: List three examples of injectable second-line antituberculosis drugs used when primary regimens fail.
back:
• Amikacin.
• Capreomycin.
• Streptomycin (classified as second-line in many modern MDR-TB protocols).

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: In the management of drug-resistant tuberculosis, the later-generation fluoroquinolones [___] and [___] are the preferred second-line oral additions.
back:
• Moxifloxacin and Levofloxacin.
• Act by inhibiting bacterial DNA gyrase.
• Essential components of MDR-TB regimens.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: A patient on a second-line TB regimen involving an analog of D-alanine develops acute psychosis and tremors. Identify the offending agent and the necessary supplement.
back:
• Cycloserine.
• Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6).
• Requires high-dose pyridoxine (100mg+) to mitigate dose-related CNS toxicity.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Describe the mechanism by which the second-line agent Ethionamide inhibits bacterial growth.
back:
• Inhibits mycolic acid synthesis.
• Chemically related to Isoniazid.
• Disrupts cell wall assembly in resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Contrast Rifampin and Rifabutin regarding their preferred use in HIV-co-infected tuberculosis patients.
back:
• Rifampin: Potent CYP450 inducer; contraindicated with most HIV protease inhibitors.
• Rifabutin: Less potent inducer; preferred second-line alternative for patients on antiretroviral therapy.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Identify the second-line agent that acts as a folate synthesis antagonist and is structurally similar to sulfonamides.
back:
• Aminosalicylic Acid (PAS).
• Inhibits dihydropteroate synthase.
• Competitive inhibitor of PABA, active almost exclusively against M. tuberculosis.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Rifampin exerts its bactericidal activity by binding to the [___] subunit of bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, thereby inhibiting RNA synthesis.
back:
• β (beta) subunit.
• Does not bind to human RNA polymerase.
• Results in inhibition of gene transcription.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: A patient shows subtherapeutic plasma levels of Isoniazid when administered in a once-weekly regimen. This pharmacokinetic variation is primarily determined by genetic polymorphism in the hepatic enzyme [___].
back:
• N-acetyltransferase.
• Rapid acetylators have half-lives <1 hour.
• Slow acetylators have half-lives of ~3 hours.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
coreConcept: Pyrazinamide Activation and Site of Action
front: Explain the specific physiological requirement for the activation of Pyrazinamide and its primary site of action within the host.
back:
• Requires acidic pH (approx. 5.5).
• Activated by mycobacterial pyrazinamidase (pncA).
• Targets mycobacteria residing within macrophage lysosomes.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Contrast the dose adjustment requirements for Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide in patients with a creatinine clearance less than 30 mL/min.
back:
• Ethambutol: Reduce dose frequency to three times weekly.
• Pyrazinamide: Dose at 25–35 mg/kg three times weekly (avoid daily use).
• Prevents accumulation and toxicity (e.g., optic neuritis or hyperuricemia).

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Specify the pharmacological effect of Rifampin on the serum concentrations of concurrent medications like methadone, warfarin, and oral contraceptives.
back:
• Significantly decreases serum levels.
• Potent induction of multiple CYP450 isoforms (3A4, 2C9, 2C19).
• May necessitate dosage increases of the affected drugs.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Ethambutol inhibits the polymerization of [___], an essential component of the mycobacterial cell wall, by targeting specific arabinosyl transferases.
back:
• Arabinoglycan.
• Encoded by the embCAB operon.
• Leads to increased cell wall permeability.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: A 50-year-old patient on anti-TB therapy presents with high-grade fever, anorexia, and right upper quadrant pain. Labs show significantly elevated AST/ALT. Which medication must be immediately and permanently discontinued?
back:
• Isoniazid (INH).
• Clinical hepatitis occurs in ~1% (higher risk with age >50 or alcohol use).
• Contrast with minor asymptomatic enzyme elevations (10-20%) which allow continuation.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Describe the molecular steps required for Isoniazid to inhibit cell wall synthesis once it has entered the mycobacterial cell.
back:
• Activated by KatG (catalase-peroxidase).
• Forms covalent complex with AcpM and KasA (beta-ketoacyl carrier protein synthetase).
• Inhibits synthesis of mycolic acids.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
coreConcept: Differential Adverse Effects of PZA and EMB
front: Differentiate between the hyperuricemia caused by Pyrazinamide and the unique optic toxicity associated with Ethambutol.
back:
• Pyrazinamide: Causes hyperuricemia in nearly all patients (inhibits renal urate excretion).
• Ethambutol: Causes retrobulbar neuritis (loss of visual acuity and red-green color blindness).
• Both are dose-dependent toxicities.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Name the harmless pharmacokinetic side effect of Rifampin that requires pre-treatment counseling regarding body fluids and accessories.
back:
• Orange discoloration of urine, sweat, and tears.
• Benign metabolite excretion.
• Can permanently stain soft contact lenses.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Standard therapy for drug-susceptible tuberculosis initiates with a 2-month intensive phase comprising four first-line agents: Isoniazid, Rifampin, Pyrazinamide, and [___].
back: • Ethambutol • First-line agents are preferred due to high bactericidal activity and well-characterized safety profiles in standard populations.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: A patient with pulmonary TB displays clinical deterioration and culture results positive for resistance to Isoniazid and Rifampin. To manage this Multidrug-Resistant (MDR) case, the clinician must select drugs from the [___] category.
back: • Second-line agents • Examples include Levofloxacin, Amikacin, and Ethionamide • MDR-TB requires longer treatment durations and medications with higher toxicity profiles.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Explain the role of the mycobacterial enzyme KatG in the activation of the first-line agent Isoniazid.
back: • KatG is a catalase-peroxidase enzyme • It activates the Isoniazid prodrug into its active moiety • This active form inhibits mycolic acid synthesis via InhA and KasA blockade.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Contrast first-line and second-line antituberculosis agents regarding their standard clinical utility in treatment-naive patients.
back: • First-line: Standard of care for all new cases due to high efficacy and manageable side effects • Second-line: Reserved for drug resistance (MDR/XDR) or first-line intolerance.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Apart from the core four first-line agents, name two other rifamycins classified as alternative or second-line agents, frequently utilized in HIV-co-infected patients.
back: • Rifabutin • Rifapentine • Rifabutin is preferred in HIV patients receiving protease inhibitors due to its lower potency for Cytochrome P450 induction.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: In the pharmacological classification of TB resistance, a strain is defined as Multidrug-Resistant (MDR-TB) based on the criterion of resistance to both [___] and [___].
back: • Isoniazid and Rifampin • This definition is the primary diagnostic criterion indicating the switch from first-line to second-line chemotherapy.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: A patient receiving multidrug TB therapy presents with burning pain in the extremities and microcytic anemia. Identify the likely first-line drug responsible and its specific preventive adjunct.
back: • Isoniazid (INH) • Prevented with Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) • INH induces competitive pyridoxine deficiency, leading to peripheral neuropathy and sideroblastic anemia.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Describe the unique sterilizing mechanism of Pyrazinamide against semi-dormant Mycobacterium tuberculosis bacilli.
back: • Converted to pyrazinoic acid by pyrazinamidase • Functions optimally in acidic environments (pH 5.5) • Specifically targets bacilli sequestered within macrophage lysosomes.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Contrast the metabolic impact of Rifampin versus Ethambutol on the hepatic Cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzyme system.
back: • Rifampin: Potent CYP450 inducer; causes significant drug-drug interactions • Ethambutol: Lacks significant impact on the Cytochrome P450 system.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Identify the novel second-line diarylquinoline that inhibits mycobacterial ATP synthase, specifically used for resistant pulmonary tuberculosis.
back: • Bedaquiline • Targets energy production by inhibiting the F0 subunit of ATP synthase • Reserved for Multidrug-Resistant cases with limited options.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: The plasma half-life of Isoniazid is primarily determined by the genetically inherited rate of the hepatic enzyme [___].
back: * N-acetyltransferase 2 (NAT2) * Distinguishes fast versus slow acetylators * Slow acetylators have a higher risk of dose-related peripheral neuropathy.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: A TB patient on a standard four-drug regimen presents with new-onset blurred vision and inability to distinguish between red and green colors. Which medication is the most likely cause?
back: * Ethambutol * Causes dose-dependent retrobulbar neuritis * Requires baseline and monthly visual acuity and color discrimination testing.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Explain the biochemical activation required for Pyrazinamide to exert its bactericidal effect within acidic macrophage lysosomes.
back: * Converted to active pyrazinoic acid * Catalyzed by mycobacterial pyrazinamidase (encoded by pncA) * Specifically targets non-replicating bacilli in acidic environments.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Contrast the effects of Rifampin and Isoniazid on the hepatic Cytochrome P450 (CYP) system regarding co-administered drugs.
back: * Rifampin: Potent inducer; decreases levels of methadone, warfarin, and protease inhibitors. * Isoniazid: Inhibitor; increases serum levels of phenytoin and carbamazepine.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Identify the specific mycobacterial cell wall component whose synthesis is blocked by the activated form of Isoniazid.
back: * Mycolic acids * Isoniazid complexes with AcpM and KasA proteins * Only occurs after KatG-mediated activation by catalase-peroxidase.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Following hepatic deacylation and secretion into the bile, Rifampin undergoes [___] recirculation to maintain therapeutic serum levels.
back: * Enterohepatic recirculation * Bulk is eventually excreted in feces * Imparts a harmless orange color to urine, sweat, and tears.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: A patient with a creatinine clearance of 25 mL/min is starting TB therapy. How must the standard administration of Pyrazinamide be modified?
back: * Reduce frequency to thrice weekly (rather than daily) * Prevents accumulation of renally-cleared metabolites * Typical dose is 25 to 35 mg/kg per session.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Describe the molecular target of Ethambutol and the resulting structural defect in the mycobacterial cell wall.
back: * Inhibits arabinosyl transferases (embCAB operon) * Blocks polymerization of arabinose into arabinogalactan * Disrupts cell wall permeability and mycolic acid attachment.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Contrast the use of Rifampin versus Rifabutin in a patient with HIV-TB co-infection receiving a protease inhibitor-based regimen.
back: * Rifabutin is preferred * It is a less potent inducer of CYP3A4 * Minimizes the risk of subtherapeutic protease inhibitor concentrations.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Name the non-hepatic metabolic laboratory abnormality that occurs in nearly all patients receiving therapeutic doses of Pyrazinamide.
back: * Hyperuricemia * Caused by inhibition of renal uric acid excretion * Usually asymptomatic and does not require cessation of therapy.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: The standard four-drug oral regimen for the intensive phase of drug-susceptible tuberculosis includes Isoniazid, Rifampin, Ethambutol, and [___].
back:
● Pyrazinamide (PZA).
● Used during the first 2 months as a sterilizing agent.
● Targets organisms in acidic environments.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: A patient failing first-line therapy is diagnosed with Multi-Drug Resistant TB (MDR-TB). The clinician adds a second-line injectable cyclic peptide protein synthesis inhibitor. Identify this drug.
back:
● Capreomycin.
● Reserved for drug-resistant cases.
● Key side effects include nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
coreConcept: Clinical Role of Second-line TB Drugs
front: Describe the rationale for restricting second-line drugs like Cycloserine or Ethionamide to specialized resistant cases rather than initial empiric therapy.
back:
● Lower clinical efficacy than first-line agents.
● Significantly higher incidence of serious toxicities (e.g., CNS psychoses, gastric irritation).
● Used primarily as alternative agents in MDR-TB management.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Contrast first-line and second-line antituberculosis agents regarding their bactericidal potency and clinical application.
back:
● First-line: Highly potent bactericidal/sterilizing agents; standard for primary susceptible infection.
● Second-line: Often less potent or more toxic; reserved for resistant strains or treatment intolerance.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Identify the second-line diarylquinoline agent that acts by inhibiting mycobacterial ATP synthase, specifically used for multi-drug resistant pulmonary cases.
back:
● Bedaquiline.
● Targets both replicating and nonreplicating bacilli.
● Novel mechanism of action introduced for resistant TB.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Among the second-line fluoroquinolones used for resistant tuberculosis, [___] is noted in UHS boards as being the most active against M. tuberculosis in vitro.
back:
● Moxifloxacin.
● Classified as a second-line agent.
● Often used in combination to manage MDR-TB.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: A 30-year-old on TB therapy develops severe retrobulbar neuritis. If the patient is moved to a second-line regimen including an oxazolidinone, which specific drug is typically selected?
back:
● Linezolid.
● Discontinue Ethambutol (source of optic neuritis).
● Linezolid provides activity against MDR-TB strains.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Explain the role of Pyrazinamide in the intensive phase of first-line therapy as a 'sterilizing agent.'
back:
● Converts to active pyrazinoic acid in acidic environments.
● Kills semi-dormant bacilli sequestered within macrophage lysosomes.
● Prevents relapse of infection.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: Contrast the use of Rifampin and Rifabutin in the classification of tuberculosis therapy for patients co-infected with HIV.
back:
● Rifampin: Standard first-line; potent CYP450 inducer.
● Rifabutin: Classified as second-line/alternative; less potent CYP induction allowing concurrent protease inhibitor use.

category: Classify antituberculosis drugs into 1st line and 2nd line agents with examples
front: List three examples of second-line antituberculosis agents that are administered via the oral route for resistant infections.
back:
● Cycloserine
● Ethionamide
● Para-aminosalicylic acid (PAS)
● Linezolid

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: The prodrug Isoniazid (INH) must be activated by the mycobacterial catalase-peroxidase enzyme known as [___] to effectively inhibit mycolic acid synthesis.
back:
- KatG.
- It converts INH into an active form that inhibits InhA and KasA enzymes.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: A patient receiving treatment for pulmonary TB develops acute gouty arthritis. This complication is most likely due to the inhibition of urate excretion by which specific drug?
back:
Pyrazinamide (PZA).
- Causes hyperuricemia uniformly.
- Usually asymptomatic, but can trigger acute gouty flares.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Describe the molecular mechanism by which Rifampin inhibits the replication of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
back:
- Binds to the beta subunit of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase.
- Inhibits RNA synthesis.
- Human RNA polymerase does not bind Rifampin.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: A patient with TB and severe renal failure (CrCl < 30 mL/min) requires dosage adjustments. Contrast the specific dosing changes needed for Ethambutol versus Pyrazinamide.
back:
- Ethambutol: Reduce frequency to three times weekly.
- Pyrazinamide: Administer 25–35 mg/kg three times weekly (not daily).

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Identify the genetic polymorphism and liver enzyme responsible for the significant variation in Isoniazid half-life between different human populations.
back:
- N-acetyltransferase (NAT2) polymorphism.
- Slow acetylators (t½ ≈ 3h) vs. Rapid acetylators (t½ < 1h).

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Ethambutol inhibits the polymerization of [___], an essential component of the mycobacterial cell wall, by targeting arabinosyl transferases.
back:
- Arabinoglycan.
- Targeted by the embCAB operon proteins.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: A TB patient presents with complete biliary obstruction. Predict the effect on Rifampin pharmacokinetics and determine if a dosage adjustment is typically required.
back:
- Effect: Serum levels may rise due to impaired biliary excretion.
- Adjustment: Standard guidelines do not require adjustment for hepatic insufficiency.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Explain how mutations resulting in the overexpression of the inhA gene provide resistance against Isoniazid.
back:
- Increases production of NADH-dependent acyl carrier protein reductase.
- Results in low-level INH resistance.
- Confers cross-resistance to Ethionamide.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Contrast the primary mycobacterial cell targets of Isoniazid and Ethambutol.
back:
- Isoniazid: Mycolic acid synthesis.
- Ethambutol: Arabinoglycan synthesis (via arabinosyl transferase).

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Identify the benign side effect of Rifampin that causes harmless discoloration of bodily secretions and requires proactive patient counseling.
back:
- Orange-to-red discoloration of urine, sweat, and tears.
- Can permanently stain soft contact lenses.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Isoniazid is a prodrug that must be activated by the mycobacterial catalase-peroxidase enzyme [___] to inhibit mycolic acid synthesis.
back:
• KatG
• Once activated, it inhibits InhA and KasA enzymes
• Disruption of mycolic acid synthesis prevents cell wall formation.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: A 45-year-old TB patient is alarmed to find his urine, tears, and sweat have turned bright orange. This pharmacokinetic phenomenon is most likely due to [___].
back:
• Rifampin
• Benign side effect of the drug's color
• Can permanently stain soft contact lenses.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Explain the role of the enzyme pyrazinamidase in the mechanism of action of Pyrazinamide.
back:
• Converted to active pyrazinoic acid by pyrazinamidase (pncA gene)
• Active only at acidic pH (approx. 5.5)
• Targets bacilli within macrophage lysosomes.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Contrast the primary sensory toxicities of Ethambutol and Isoniazid regarding their clinical presentation.
back:
• Ethambutol: Retrobulbar neuritis (decreased visual acuity, red-green color blindness)
• Isoniazid: Peripheral neuropathy (paresthesias, numbness in hands/feet).

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: The wide inter-patient variability in Isoniazid plasma half-life is primarily attributed to a genetic polymorphism in the hepatic enzyme [___].
back:
• N-acetyltransferase (NAT2)
• Classified into 'Rapid' and 'Slow' acetylators
• Slow acetylators have increased risk of neuropathy/toxicity.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Ethambutol selectively disrupts the mycobacterial cell wall by inhibiting [___], which prevents the polymerization of arabinoglycan.
back:
• Arabinosyl transferases
• Encoded by the embCAB operon
• Resistance occurs via mutations in the embB gene.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: A patient on a standard 4-drug TB regimen develops acute arthralgia and podagra. The drug responsible likely interferes with the renal excretion of [___].
back:
• Uric acid (Hyperuricemia)
• Caused by Pyrazinamide (PZA)
• Asymptomatic elevation is common; gout is less frequent.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Describe the molecular basis for Rifampin resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
back:
• Point mutations in the rpoB gene
• Alters the beta subunit of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
• Results in reduced drug binding affinity.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Differentiate the cytochrome P450 induction properties of Rifampin versus Rifabutin in HIV co-infection.
back:
• Rifampin: Potent inducer of multiple CYP isoforms; contraindicates most PIs
• Rifabutin: Less potent inducer; preferred in HIV patients on PIs or INSTIs.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Identify the vitamin supplement required during Isoniazid therapy and its biochemical rationale.
back:
• Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6)
• INH promotes pyridoxine excretion and inhibits pyridoxal kinase
• Prevents INH-induced peripheral neuropathy.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Isoniazid prevents mycobacterial cell wall synthesis by primarily inhibiting the enzyme [___], which is required for the production of essential mycolic acids.
back:
• InhA (NADH-dependent acyl carrier protein reductase).
• This action blocks the assembly of the mycolic acid layer.
• The drug must first be activated by the bacterial catalase-peroxidase enzyme, KatG.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: A 45-year-old patient undergoing intensive phase TB therapy is concerned that his urine and sweat have turned a bright orange-red color. Identify the drug responsible and the clinical significance of this finding.
back:
• Rifampin.
• This is a harmless, expected side effect of the medication.
• It occurs because the drug is an inherently orange-red compound excreted in most body fluids.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Explain how Ethambutol disrupts the structural integrity of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis cell wall.
back:
• Inhibits arabinosyl transferases (encoded by the embCAB operon).
• This disruption halts the polymerization of arabinoglycan.
• Leads to increased cell wall permeability and inhibition of mycobacterial growth.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Contrast the effects of Isoniazid and Rifampin on the hepatic Cytochrome P450 enzyme system regarding drug-drug interactions.
back:
• Rifampin: Potent inducer of multiple CYP isoforms (lowers levels of concurrent drugs like methadone or anticoagulants).
• Isoniazid: Functions primarily as an inhibitor of certain CYP enzymes (can raise levels of drugs like phenytoin).

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Identify the specific intracellular environment and metabolic role that makes Pyrazinamide a "sterilizing" agent in TB therapy.
back:
• Acts specifically in acidic environments (macrophage lysosomes).
• Kills non-replicating, dormant bacilli sequestered within acidic vacuoles.
• Its use is essential for shortening total treatment duration to 6 months.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: The dose-dependent adverse effect of Ethambutol that necessitates baseline and monthly monitoring of visual acuity and color discrimination is [___].
back:
• Retrobulbar neuritis.
• Clinical signs include decreased visual acuity and loss of red-green color perception.
• Generally reversible if the drug is discontinued promptly.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: An alcoholic patient being treated for pulmonary TB develops tingling and numbness in his hands and feet. State the drug involved and the biochemical rationale for the corrective supplement needed.
back:
• Isoniazid.
• The drug promotes the excretion of Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6).
• Administering B6 prevents peripheral neuropathy by restoring the essential cofactor levels.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Describe the specific molecular target alteration that leads to high-level Rifampin resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
back:
• Point mutations in the rpoB gene.
• This gene encodes the beta subunit of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase.
• Mutations significantly reduce the binding affinity of Rifampin to the RNA polymerase enzyme.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Distinguish between "slow acetylators" and "fast acetylators" in the context of Isoniazid metabolism.
back:
• Based on genetically determined levels of hepatic N-acetyltransferase.
• Slow acetylators: Higher plasma levels and longer half-life; increased risk of toxicity.
• Fast acetylators: Lower plasma levels; may require higher frequency dosing.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Name the active form of Pyrazinamide and the specific enzyme responsible for its conversion within the mycobacterial cell.
back:
• Active form: Pyrazinoic acid.
• Enzyme: Pyrazinamidase (encoded by the pncA gene).
• Resistance often arises from mutations in this activating gene.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Isoniazid requires initial activation by the mycobacterial enzyme [___] to form a covalent complex that inhibits mycolic acid synthesis.
back:
• Enzyme: KatG (catalase-peroxidase)
• Target: Blocks InhA and KasA (ketoacyl carrier protein synthetase)
• Effect: Disrupts cell wall assembly

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
coreConcept: Rifampin Mechanism and Benign Side Effects
front: A 45-year-old male with pulmonary TB on a standard four-drug regimen notes orange discoloration of his sweat and tears. The drug responsible for this acts by inhibiting [___].
back:
• Drug: Rifampin
• Mechanism: Inhibits the β-subunit of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
• Note: Prevents RNA synthesis; discoloration is benign and expected

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Explain the pharmacodynamic role of Pyrazinamide during the initial intensive phase of tuberculosis treatment.
back:
• Function: Acts as a 'sterilizing agent'
• Environment: Targets semi-dormant bacilli in acidic environments (macrophage lysosomes)
• Efficacy: Essential for shortening total treatment from 9 to 6 months

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Contrast the primary resistance mechanisms of Isoniazid involving the katG gene versus the inhA gene.
back:
• katG: Deletion or mutation prevents prodrug activation (high-level resistance)
• inhA: Promoter mutations cause enzyme overexpression (low-level resistance)
• Cross-resistance: inhA mutations often confer cross-resistance to ethionamide

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Explain the pharmacokinetic rationale for adjusting Ethambutol dosage in patients with a creatinine clearance less than 30 mL/min.
back:
• Elimination: 50% excreted unchanged in urine
• Accumulation Risk: Decreased renal clearance leads to toxic drug levels
• Toxicity: Increases the risk of dose-related retrobulbar neuritis

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Ethambutol achieves its bacteriostatic effect by inhibiting [___], disrupting the polymerization of the mycobacterial cell wall component arabinoglycan.
back:
• Target: Arabinosyl transferases (encoded by the embCAB operon)
• Spectrum: Active against M. tuberculosis and M. kansasii
• Level: Bacteriostatic (not bactericidal)

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: A TB patient on Rifampin and Isoniazid is prescribed Warfarin for a DVT. Describe the pharmacokinetic interaction that necessitates an increase in the Warfarin dose.
back:
• Interaction: Rifampin is a potent inducer of multiple Cytochrome P450 isoforms (CYP3A4, 2C9)
• Effect: Accelerated metabolism and clearance of Warfarin
• Consequence: Decreased serum concentrations and reduced anticoagulant efficacy

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Describe the intracellular metabolic conversion required for Pyrazinamide to exert its antimicrobial effect.
back:
• Conversion: Prodrug converted to active Pyrazinoic acid
• Enzyme: Mycobacterial pyrazinamidase (encoded by pncA)
• Mechanism: Active acid disrupts cell membrane potential and transport functions

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Contrast the pharmacokinetics of Isoniazid in 'fast' versus 'slow' acetylators regarding the risk of clinical complications.
back:
• Fast Acetylators: Higher clearance; risk of subtherapeutic levels if dosed intermittently
• Slow Acetylators: Drug accumulation risk
• Toxicity: Slow acetylators are more prone to dose-related peripheral neuropathy

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Identify the bacterial enzyme target that explains Rifampin’s selective toxicity over human cells.
back:
• Target: Bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
• Selectivity: Human RNA polymerase does not bind Rifampin
• Result: Bacterial transcription is inhibited without affecting host cell transcription

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Isoniazid is a prodrug that must be activated by the mycobacterial enzyme [___] to inhibit the synthesis of mycolic acids.
back:
• KatG (catalase-peroxidase)
• Activated drug inhibits AcpM and KasA
• Prevents formation of essential mycobacterial cell wall components.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: A 45-year-old patient on TB therapy presents with orange-colored urine, sweat, and tears. Identify the drug responsible and its primary pharmacokinetic interaction with human metabolic enzymes.
back:
• Rifampin
• Potent inducer of Cytochrome P450 isoforms (CYP3A4, 2C9, 2C19, etc.)
• Significantly increases the elimination of medications like methadone and oral contraceptives.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Explain the specific biochemical pathway inhibited by Ethambutol and the resulting effect on the mycobacterial cell wall.
back:
• Inhibits arabinosyl transferases (encoded by the embCAB operon)
• Blocks the polymerization of arabinoglycan
• Disrupts cell wall integrity, leading to bacteriostatic effects.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
coreConcept: Anti-TB Drug Dosing in Renal Failure
front: Contrast Pyrazinamide and Ethambutol regarding their specific dosing adjustments required for patients with a creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min.
back:
• Pyrazinamide: Reduce to 25–35 mg/kg three times weekly (to prevent metabolite accumulation).
• Ethambutol: Reduce to 15–25 mg/kg three times weekly (to avoid retrobulbar neuritis toxicity).

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Identify the genetic factor determining the plasma half-life of Isoniazid and the specific toxicity associated with its deficiency.
back:
• Liver N-acetyltransferase (Fast vs. Slow acetylators)
• Induces Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) deficiency
• Causes peripheral neuropathy, which is reversed by Vitamin B6 supplementation.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Pyrazinamide functions as a 'sterilizing' agent by effectively killing residual intracellular mycobacteria residing within the [___] environment of lysosomes.
back:
• Acidic (Low pH)
• Converted to active pyrazinoic acid by mycobacterial pyrazinamidase (pncA)
• Essential for shortening TB treatment duration to 6 months.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: A patient undergoing TB treatment experiences blurred vision and an inability to distinguish between red and green colors. Name the causative agent and the necessary clinical monitoring.
back:
• Ethambutol
• Causes dose-related retrobulbar neuritis
• Requires baseline and monthly visual acuity and color discrimination testing.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: How does Rifampin carry out its bactericidal effect and what specific genetic mutation is responsible for high-level bacterial resistance?
back:
• Binds to the β subunit of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
• Inhibits bacterial RNA synthesis
• Resistance: Point mutations in the rpoB gene (reduced drug binding).

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Contrast Rifampin and Rifabutin regarding their therapeutic role in patients co-infected with HIV who are receiving protease inhibitors.
back:
• Rifampin: Potent CYP inducer; significantly lowers protease inhibitor levels (contraindicated).
• Rifabutin: Less potent CYP inducer; preferred alternative in HIV-TB co-infection
• Prevents subtherapeutic antiretroviral levels.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Identify the metabolic abnormality uniformly produced by Pyrazinamide and its clinical significance.
back:
• Hyperuricemia (elevated serum uric acid)
• Usually asymptomatic and does not require treatment cessation
• Occurs because Pyrazinamide inhibits uric acid excretion.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Isoniazid is a prodrug that must be activated by the mycobacterial enzyme [___] to effectively inhibit the synthesis of mycolic acids.
back:
• Catalase-peroxidase (KatG)
• Target: InhA and KasA
• Result: Disruption of the mycobacterial cell wall structural integrity.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: A 50-year-old TB patient develops symmetrical numbness and tingling in his extremities. This clinical finding is physiologically caused by [___].
back:
• Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) deficiency
• Mechanism: INH promotes Vitamin B6 excretion
• Management: Prevented by oral Pyridoxine supplementation.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Explain the role of the intracellular environment in the pharmacodynamic efficacy of Pyrazinamide.
back:
• Active at acidic pH (5.5)
• Targets bacilli within macrophage lysosomes
• Mechanism: Converted to pyrazinoic acid by pyrazinamidase (pncA).

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: A patient on ATT presents with red-green color blindness and a decrease in visual acuity. Contrast the drug causing this with the agent that causes harmless orange discoloration of secretions.
back:
• Ethambutol: Causes dose-related retrobulbar neuritis (visual loss)
• Rifampin: Induces harmless orange sweat, tears, and urine
• Clinical: EMB requires baseline visual testing.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Identify the hepatic metabolic process responsible for the bimodal distribution (fast vs. slow) of Isoniazid plasma half-life.
back:
• Acetylation
• Enzyme: N-acetyltransferase
• Clinical: Slow acetylators have increased risk of INH-induced peripheral neuropathy.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: Rifampin exerts its bactericidal effect by binding to the [___] subunit of bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase.
back:
• Beta (β) subunit
• Effect: Inhibition of RNA synthesis
• Resistance: Point mutations in the rpoB gene.

category: Describe the characteristic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic properties of Rifampin, Isoniazid, Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
front: An HIV-positive patient on Protease Inhibitors develops TB. Explain the pharmacokinetic rationale for preferring Rifabutin over Rifampin in this patient.
