- Streptomycin: Mutations in rpsL (S12 protein) or rrs (16S rRNA)
- Amikacin: Low cross-resistance with Streptomycin; primarily different ribosomal binding modifications

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Specify the primary reason the theoretically optimal 1g/d dose of Ethionamide is rarely achievable in clinical practice for MDR-TB patients.
back:
- Severe gastric irritation and neurologic symptoms
- Limit tolerable dose to 500–750 mg daily
- Hepatotoxicity is also dose-related

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Para-aminosalicylic acid (PAS) delayed-release granules must be administered by sprinkling them over [___] to protect the integrity of their acid-resistant coating.
back:
• Acidic foods like applesauce or yogurt.
• Alternatively swirled in fruit juice.
• Prevents premature degradation and GI irritation.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: A patient undergoing therapy for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) develops acute depression and tremors. Which second-line agent is the most likely cause?
back:
• Cycloserine.
• Causes dose-related CNS toxicity.
• Manifests as psychosis, seizures, or suicidal ideation.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Explain the molecular mechanism of cross-resistance between the novel agent Bedaquiline and Clofazimine.
back:
• Upregulation of the MmpL5 multisubstrate efflux pump.
• Reduces effective intracellular concentrations of both drugs.
• Affects treatment efficacy in MDR-TB.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Contrast the management of neurologic side effects in Ethionamide therapy versus Cycloserine therapy.
back:
• Ethionamide: Symptoms alleviated by Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6).
• Cycloserine: Ameliorated by high-dose Pyridoxine (100mg+) and monitoring peak levels (20–35 mcg/mL).

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Which laboratory parameter must be closely monitored weekly for a patient receiving Linezolid for MDR-TB to detect its primary reversible toxicity?
back:
• Complete Blood Count (CBC).
• Monitors for bone marrow suppression.
• Specifically identifies thrombocytopenia, anemia, and neutropenia.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: High-level resistance to the second-line injectable agent Capreomycin is primarily associated with mutations in the [___] genes.
back:
• rrs, eis, or tlyA genes.
• Alters the ribosomal binding site or drug modification.
• Often presents in multidrug-resistant strains.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: A patient on MDR-TB therapy presents with visual blurring and red-green color blindness. If they are already taking Ethambutol, which second-line agent could potentially add to this optic neuritis risk?
back:
• Rifabutin, Linezolid, or Ethionamide.
• All have been reported to cause optic neuritis.
• Mandates immediate visual assessment and drug review.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Why is Bedaquiline specifically administered with a high-fat meal?
back:
• Increases oral bioavailability.
• Fat doubles the peak plasma concentration (Cmax) and total exposure (AUC).
• Essential for achieving therapeutic levels against replicating bacilli.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Contrast the target serum peak/trough levels for Amikacin when used in MDR-TB therapy.
back:
• Target Peak: 30–45 mcg/mL.
• Target Trough: Undetectable/Zero.
• Measured 30–60 minutes post-dose to ensure efficacy and limit nephrotoxicity.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: What cardiac abnormality is a major concern when co-administering Fluoroquinolones (e.g., Moxifloxacin) and Bedaquiline?
back:
• QTc interval prolongation.
• Increases risk of Torsades de Pointes.
• Requires baseline and periodic ECG monitoring.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: The second-line antituberculosis agent that specifically targets and inhibits mycobacterial ATP synthase is [___].
back:
● Bedaquiline
● Used for pulmonary MDR-TB when other options are unavailable
● Novel diarylquinoline class with a long terminal half-life of 5.5 months

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: A patient undergoing treatment for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis develops severe gastric irritation and depression. This clinical profile is most consistent with the use of [___].
back:
● Ethionamide
● Chemically related to Isoniazid; blocks mycolic acid synthesis
● Often limits tolerable dose to 500–750 mg due to GI and neurologic side effects

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Explain the role of Bedaquiline in MDR-TB therapy regarding its black-box warning and cardiac monitoring.
back:
● Risk: Significant QTc interval prolongation
● Monitoring: Baseline and serial EKGs required
● Caution: Avoid in patients with existing cardiac conduction abnormalities or increased mortality risks

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Contrast the hematologic and neurologic toxicities associated with prolonged Linezolid use in MDR-TB management.
back:
● Hematologic: Reversible bone marrow suppression and thrombocytopenia
● Neurologic: Irreversible peripheral and optic neuropathy
● Prevention: Supplemental pyridoxine is often recommended despite the risk of permanent damage

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Specify the dosing adjustment required for Ethionamide to minimize its common neurologic and gastrointestinal adverse effects.
back:
● Dose Escalation: Start at 250 mg once daily, increasing in 250 mg increments
● Adjunct: Administer with Pyridoxine to alleviate neurologic symptoms
● Target: Optimal adult dose is 1 g/d (often restricted to 500-750 mg)

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: To mitigate the risk of depression, psychosis, and seizures during Cycloserine therapy, patients must concurrently receive [___].
back:
● Pyridoxine (100 mg or more per day)
● Ameliorates dose-related central nervous system toxicity
● Monitoring peak serum concentrations (target 20–35 mcg/mL) further reduces adverse events

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: A patient with MDR-TB is prescribed an oral agent to be sprinkled on applesauce. If the patient develops fever, joint pain, and hepatosplenomegaly after 4 weeks, the likely culprit is [___].
back:
● Aminosalicylic acid (PAS)
● Folate synthesis antagonist (PABA analog)
● Causes common GI distress and serious hypersensitivity reactions in 3–8 weeks

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Describe the mechanism of action of Capreomycin and its primary route of administration in MDR-TB cases.
back:
● Mechanism: Peptide protein synthesis inhibitor
● Route: Intramuscular or intravenous injection
● Toxicity: Significant nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity (tinnitus, vestibular disturbances)

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Contrast the use of Rifabutin versus Rifampin in the context of HIV co-infection and protease inhibitor therapy.
back:
● Rifabutin: Less potent CYP450 inducer; preferred with protease inhibitors
● Rifampin: Strong inducer; markedly reduces serum levels of most HIV medications
● Both: Subject to cross-resistance via rpoB gene mutations

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: What is the primary pharmacological advantage of utilizing later-generation fluoroquinolones (e.g., Moxifloxacin) in MDR-TB regimens?
back:
● Increased potency against M. tuberculosis (Moxifloxacin is the most active in vitro)
● Useful against strains resistant to first-line agents
● Must be used in combination to prevent rapid emergence of resistance

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: The second-line antituberculosis agent [___] is a structural analog of D-alanine that acts by inhibiting alanine racemase and can cause dose-related acute psychosis.
back:
• Cycloserine.
• Inhibits D-alanyl-D-alanine ligase.
• Adverse effects include tremors, convulsions, and severe CNS toxicity.
• Pyridoxine (100 mg/d) helps ameliorate neurologic symptoms.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: A patient undergoing treatment for MDR-TB reports severe gastric irritation and a persistent, distressing metallic taste in the mouth. These findings suggest the use of [___].
back:
• Ethionamide.
• A chemical relative of Isoniazid that blocks mycolic acid synthesis.
• Frequently poorly tolerated due to intense GI irritation and neurologic symptoms.
• Also carries a risk of hepatotoxicity.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Describe the molecular mechanism by which Bedaquiline inhibits the growth of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
back:
• Inhibits mycobacterial ATP synthase.
• Specifically targets the C-subunit of the ATP synthase proton pump.
• Active against both replicating and nonreplicating (dormant) bacilli.
• First drug with a novel mechanism approved in decades.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Contrast Capreomycin and Amikacin regarding their drug class and the typical pattern of cross-resistance with Streptomycin in TB therapy.
back:
• Capreomycin is a peptide protein synthesis inhibitor; Amikacin is an aminoglycoside.
• Streptomycin-resistant strains often remain susceptible to Capreomycin.
• Capreomycin typically shows cross-resistance with Amikacin and Kanamycin via rrs gene mutations.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Specify the unique administration requirement for Aminosalicylic Acid (PAS) granules and the clinical rationale behind this method.
back:
• Sprinkled on acidic food (applesauce/yogurt) or swirled in juice.
• Must be swallowed whole without chewing.
• Rationale: Protects the acid-sensitive delayed-release coating to ensure drug reaching the small intestine.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: A patient on long-term MDR-TB therapy develops duration-dependent bone marrow suppression and optic neuropathy. These adverse effects are classically linked to the agent [___].
back:
• Linezolid.
• Inhibits protein synthesis at the 50S subunit.
• Toxicities result from inhibition of mitochondrial protein synthesis.
• Optic and peripheral neuropathy may be irreversible.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: A patient with MDR-TB develops a systemic syndrome featuring fever, joint pain, and hepatosplenomegaly after 4 weeks of therapy with an anti-folate granules. Identify the likely diagnosis and required intervention.
back:
• PAS-induced Hypersensitivity Reaction.
• Occurs typically between 3–8 weeks of therapy.
• Intervention: Permanent discontinuation of Aminosalicylic Acid (PAS).
• Can manifest as granulocytopenia or hepatitis if continued.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Describe the therapeutic role and dosing considerations for Moxifloxacin within a multidrug-resistant tuberculosis regimen.
back:
• Targets DNA gyrase (A subunit) to inhibit DNA replication.
• Most active fluoroquinolone against M. tuberculosis in vitro.
• Must be used in combination with 2+ other active agents to prevent rapid resistance.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Contrast the cardiac safety profile of Bedaquiline with that of first-line antituberculosis agents.
back:
• Bedaquiline carries a Black Box warning for QTc interval prolongation.
• First-line agents (INH, RIF) are primarily hepatotoxic, not cardiotoxic.
• Requires baseline and periodic EKG monitoring; used only when no other options exist.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Identify the primary clinical indication for Clofazimine and its most characteristic dermatologic side effect when used for salvage TB therapy.
back:
• Indication: Multibacillary Leprosy (primary) and salvage therapy for MDR-TB.
• Side effect: Red-to-brown discoloration of the skin and conjunctivae.
• Results from drug accumulation in reticuloendothelial tissues.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: The neuropsychiatric adverse effects of Cycloserine in MDR-TB therapy are managed by the co-administration of [___] at doses of 100mg or more daily.
back:
● Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6).
● Ameliorates symptoms like depression, psychoses, and seizures.
● Required due to Cycloserine’s interference with B6-dependent enzymes.
● Essential for maintaining CNS function during therapy.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: A patient on MDR-TB therapy develops fever, joint pain, hepatosplenomegaly, and a skin rash 5 weeks after starting a granular medication taken with applesauce. Identify the causative agent.
back:
● Aminosalicylic Acid (PAS).
● Hypersensitivity reactions typically occur 3-8 weeks into therapy.
● Granule formulations improve GI tolerance but still commonly cause nausea and vomiting.
● Requires discontinuation if systemic hypersensitivity develops.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Describe the molecular mechanism by which Capreomycin exerts its therapeutic effect against resistant mycobacteria.
back:
● Inhibits protein synthesis by binding to the 70S ribosomal unit.
● Acts specifically against extracellular bacilli.
● No cross-resistance with Streptomycin.
● Potential cross-resistance exists with Amikacin and Kanamycin.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Contrast Linezolid and Bedaquiline regarding their primary dose-limiting systemic toxicities during long-term MDR-TB management.
back:
● Linezolid: Irreversible peripheral and optic neuropathy; bone marrow suppression.
● Bedaquiline: QTc interval prolongation (cardiac toxicity) and hepatotoxicity.
● Bedaquiline carries an FDA black-box warning for increased mortality.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Why is Ethionamide considered a prodrug in the treatment of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis?
back:
● Requires activation by the EthA monooxygenase enzyme.
● Once activated, it inhibits mycolic acid synthesis via the InhA pathway.
● Structurally related to isoniazid but requires different enzymatic activation.
● Used when high-level isoniazid resistance is present.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Aminosalicylic acid (PAS) is a folate synthesis antagonist that acts as a structural analog of [___].
back:
● Para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA).
● Competitively inhibits dihydropteroate synthase.
● Highly specific for Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
● Displays minimal activity against other mycobacterial or bacterial species.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: A 60-year-old MDR-TB patient experiences persistent tinnitus and a rising serum creatinine level after 2 months of an injectable second-line agent. Which drug is most likely responsible?
back:
● Amikacin (or Kanamycin).
● Aminoglycosides cause dose-related auditory ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity.
● Requires monitoring of peak/trough serum concentrations.
● Requires dosage adjustment based on creatinine clearance.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Explain how Bedaquiline causes mycobacterial death in non-replicating (dormant) bacilli.
back:
● Inhibits ATP synthase.
● Blocks the mycobacterial proton pump required for energy production.
● Effective against both replicating and non-replicating (latent) mycobacteria.
● Represents a novel diarylquinoline class with unique metabolic targeting.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: Contrast the targets of Cycloserine and Ethionamide in the synthesis of the mycobacterial cell envelope.
back:
● Cycloserine: Inhibits cell wall synthesis by acting as a D-alanine analog.
● Ethionamide: Inhibits mycolic acid synthesis via the InhA reductase.
● Both are bacteriostatic and target separate structural components.

category: Discuss 2nd line drugs used in treatment of multidrug resistant tuberculosis with their therapeutic and adverse effects
front: What adjunctive vitamin supplementation is recommended for patients receiving Linezolid to mitigate hematologic or neurologic side effects?
back:
● Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6).
● Reduces the risk of peripheral neuropathy and anemia.
● Indicated for prolonged Linezolid courses exceeding 28 days.
● Helps prevent mitochondrial protein synthesis inhibition in host cells.
